subject: Future Tech
title: Recycling Air and Water
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Recycling Air and Water.

hook.text: The ISS recycles almost every drop of water, including sweat and urine.

buildup.text: The Environmental Control and Life Support System on the ISS recovers about 90% of water from humidity and waste.

discovery.text: Electrolysis splits recycled water into oxygen for breathing and hydrogen, which is vented or used as fuel.

twist.text: Even 90% isn't enough for a Mars colony. Any loss compounds. Colonists need near-perfect 98%+ recycling to survive.

climax.text: Bioregenerative systems use algae and plants to close the loop, producing oxygen and food while consuming CO2 and waste.

punchline.text: In space, nothing is waste. Everything is supply.

quiz.question: What does the ISS use electrolysis to produce from recycled water?
